# Knowing {#knowing}

English *I think* can be a guess, a memory, or a conclusion from clues, and the listener has to work out which. Ageben keeps the ordinary verb and adds a `/th/` stance word that says which: MAY for what could be so, or a word for how you know it. So a guess never passes for a report, and a report says what it rests on.

### MAY {#may}
<!-- Agent summary: MAY = `oma` + ending as a `/th/` stance word: "could be so"; claims neither that it happens nor why you think so. Default `thomam`. Contrast: `zalazun thomam dahelan vudurul.` (may be leaving) vs `zalazun dahelan vudurul.` (reported as happening). Matters most for painful guesses (rejection, blow, loss). A later plain sentence settles the guess, never contradicts it. *I think* as a guess → MAY (test: *could be* fits in its place); *I think* as the act of thinking → verb `vevemel` (`zazozon vevemel.`). Noun `zomal` = a thought. Claims only: no reading on a command, request or prohibition, so leave it off them (it does not soften `yol vowurol.`). -->

English *maybe* and *I think* let you say something *could be* so without claiming that it is: *Alazun may be leaving*. Ageben keeps the ordinary sentence and adds one [stance](clause.md#stance-th) word, the `/th/` word that says how you stand toward the whole claim. For a guess, that word is **`oma`** plus an ending, and it is called **MAY**. The sentence then says the leaving is possible, not that it happens, and it gives no reason for thinking so. (cue: same root as `omal` *thought*: a *may* is a thought about the scene, not a report of it)

> `zalazun thomam dahelan vudurul.`
>
> z-Alazun | th-MAY | d-Ahelan | v-departure
>
> "Alazun may be leaving Ahelan."

Start with **`thomam`**, *may* / *could be*, as here. Take the `/th/` word out and the same words make a report:

> `zalazun dahelan vudurul.`
>
> z-Alazun | d-Ahelan | v-departure
>
> "Alazun is leaving Ahelan."

Without the `/th/` word, you are reporting that it happens. With `thomam`, you claim only that it could. This matters most for painful guesses (a rejection, a blow, a loss), because English *I think* easily turns them into facts.

A later plain sentence does not contradict a *may*. Suppose you said `zalazun thomam dahelan vudurul.` and then found out that Alazun is leaving. Saying `zalazun dahelan vudurul.` settles the guess, and so would saying that Alazun is not leaving, since MAY never claimed either.

English *I think* has two uses, and only one of them is MAY. In *I think Alazun is leaving*, it marks a guess. In *Azozon is thinking about the trip*, it describes something Azozon is doing. To tell them apart, put *could be* in place of *I think*: if the meaning stays the same, the sentence is a guess and takes MAY. As a plain noun the root keeps its own meaning (`zomal` *a thought*); the verb *think* is a different root, `vevemel`.

**Compare with:** `zazozon vevemel.` is *Azozon thinks*, a report of the act of thinking; it does not mark anything as a guess.

MAY goes only on a claim, a sentence that says how things are or could be. A [command, request, or prohibition](/speech-moves#speech-act-beginner) tells someone what to do or not to do, so it is not a claim, and MAY has no reading there. For example, MAY does not turn the command `yol vowurol.` (*Walk!*) into a gentler suggestion. Leave it off, and give the command as it is.

### Follow-up endings (MAY) {#follow-up-endings-may}
<!-- Agent summary: ending on MAY = follow-up on the guess. `thomal` (`-l`): you will find out; `thomam` (`-m`, default): follow-up unstated, use when unsure; `thomar` (`-r`): passing thought, not pursuing it. None is better. Contrast set: `zahelan thomal vagamul.`, `zahelan thomam vagamul.`, `zahelan thomar vagamul.` `-n` → ordinary name. Yes/no question + MAY asks whether it could be so: `yel zazozon vabuvul thomal dalazun.` (might Azozon be punching Alazun? let's find out) vs `yel zazozon vabuvul dalazun.` (is Azozon punching Alazun?); `thomal` on a question = asking in order to find out. -->

After a guess, English often adds what you mean to do about it: *I'll find out*, or *who knows*. In Ageben the ending on MAY says this, so the guess and your follow-up stay one word. With `-l` you will find out, with `-m` you leave that unsaid (the default), and with `-r` it is a passing thought you are not pursuing. With `-n`, the word is an ordinary name.

| Ageben | Use | English | Same root as | Cue |
|--------|-----|---------|--------------|-----|
| **`thomal`** | could be, and you are committed to settling it | *may, I'll find out* / *let's find out* | `omal` *thought* | 💭: balloon plus a magnifying glass (`-l` the full run) |
| **`thomam`** | could be (default; follow-up unstated) | *may* / *could be* | `omal` *thought* | 💭: balloon (`-m` middle) |
| **`thomar`** | could be, as a passing thought you are not pursuing right now | *may, who knows* | `omal` *thought* | 💭: balloon drifting off (`-r` ≈ right now) |

Here is the same guess with each ending:

> `zahelan thomal vagamul.`
>
> z-Ahelan | th-MAY-find-out | v-cry
>
> "Ahelan may be crying, I'll find out."

> `zahelan thomam vagamul.`
>
> z-Ahelan | th-MAY | v-cry
>
> "Ahelan may be crying."

> `zahelan thomar vagamul.`
>
> z-Ahelan | th-MAY-who-knows | v-cry
>
> "Ahelan may be crying, who knows."

All three say that Ahelan could be crying, and only the ending changes. With `thomal`, you will find out, for example by going to look. With `thomam`, you say nothing about a next step. With `thomar`, you have considered it and are letting it go for now. To keep the three in order, read them as one line from a guess you will see through to the end (`-l`), through the middle (`-m`), to a thought that holds only right now (`-r`).

No ending is better than the others: finding out, leaving it at *may*, and letting it go are all fine choices, so pick the ending that matches what you will do. When you are not sure, use `thomam`: it says *could be* and nothing about following up.

> `zalazun thomal dazozon vabuvul.`
>
> z-Alazun | th-MAY-find-out | d-Azozon | v-punch
>
> "Alazun may be punching Azozon, I'll find out."

A yes/no question, the kind a turn starting with `yel` asks, works the same way. Without MAY, it asks whether something is so:

> `yel zazozon vabuvul dalazun.`
>
> y-question | z-Azozon | v-punch | d-Alazun
>
> "Is Azozon punching Alazun?"

With MAY, it asks whether it could be so, not whether it is. With `thomal`, it also says you are asking in order to find out:

> `yel zazozon vabuvul thomal dalazun.`
>
> y-question | z-Azozon | v-punch | th-MAY-find-out | d-Alazun
>
> "Might Azozon be punching Alazun? Let's find out."

### Live vs memory {#live-vs-memory}
<a id="memory-record"></a>
<a id="memory"></a>
<a id="record-past"></a>
<a id="live"></a>
<a id="reconstructive-catch"></a>
<!-- Agent summary: evidential = `/th/` stance word naming the channel a claim reached you through. `thugem` LIVE: in your senses as you speak, any sense (sight, sound, touch, an ache) → present; `thevum` MEMORY: you remember sensing it → past. Verbs have no past or future form, so the channel places the event in time: `zazozon thugem vowurol.` = is walking, I see it; `zazozon thevum vowurol.` = walked, I remember. Nothing behind the claim → MAY (`thomam`). Never both on one claim. Seeing as an act = verb `vayebel` (`zazozon thevum dunobal vayebel.` = Azozon saw a boot, as I remember); *I witnessed it* → MEMORY. Screen or recording: `thugem` while you watch, `thevum` after, device as `bl-` partner (`thugem blugewel` / `thevum blugewel`). -->

English often says how you know a claim: *I see it*, *I saw it*. Ageben keeps the ordinary verb and adds a `/th/` stance word for that, called an **evidential**. It names the **channel** the claim reached you through: **LIVE** if the scene is in your senses as you speak, **MEMORY** if you remember sensing it. Verbs have no past or future form, so these two channels also place the event in time: a MEMORY claim is past.

> `zazozon thugem vowurol.`
>
> z-Azozon | th-LIVE | v-walk
>
> "Azozon is walking, I can see it."

> `zazozon thevum vowurol.`
>
> z-Azozon | th-MEMORY | v-walk
>
> "Azozon walked, I remember it."

Only the stance word differs between these two. With `thugem`, Azozon is walking now and you are watching. With `thevum`, the walking is over and you remember it. The verb `vowurol` is the same in both, so the English *is walking* and *walked* both come from the channel word.

These two channels are enough for ordinary talk about a scene in your senses. To choose, ask whether the scene is in view, in earshot, or on your skin as you speak: if it is, use `thugem`, and if you are recalling it, use `thevum`.

**For *could be* with nothing behind it, use:** [MAY](#may).

> `zazozon thomam vowurol.`
>
> z-Azozon | th-MAY | v-walk
>
> "Azozon may be walking."

The same sentence with `thomam` says only that Azozon could be walking. It names no channel, because MAY gives no reason for thinking so. So use LIVE or MEMORY when you sensed the scene yourself, and MAY when you have nothing behind the claim.

| Ageben | Use | English | Same root as | Cue |
|--------|-----|---------|--------------|-----|
| **`thugem`** | LIVE: firsthand, sensed now, by any sense | *live* / *from the scene* | `ugel` *attest* | 👁️‍🗨️: sensing-and-saying while it is in view, in earshot, or on your skin |
| **`thevum`** | MEMORY: firsthand, remembered | *I remember* / *from memory* | `evul` *fishing* | 🎣: you pull something back |

LIVE covers every sense, not only sight: a sound in earshot, cold on your skin, an ache in your knee. MEMORY is the same senses, remembered.

**Compare with:** the act of seeing is the ordinary verb `vayebel`; LIVE only says how you know the claim.

English *I see it* and *I saw it* both report watching; they differ in when you watched, which is the split between LIVE and MEMORY. Do not put both on one claim. English *I witnessed it* is MEMORY, because the witnessing is over by the time you tell it. (cue: same root as `evul` *fishing*: remembering pulls the episode back up, and what comes up may not be what you hoped, the way a line can come up with a boot)

> `zazozon thevum dunobal vayebel.`
>
> z-Azozon | th-MEMORY | d-boot | v-see
>
> "Azozon saw a boot, as I remember it."

In this sentence the seeing is Azozon's, and it is part of the claim, so it is the verb `vayebel`. How you know the claim is a separate matter, and `thevum` says it: you remember the scene of Azozon seeing the boot.

A screen or a recording extends your senses. While you watch footage, it is LIVE with the device as the source; once you have watched it, it is MEMORY, because your memory of the footage can slip just as a memory of the scene can. In the examples below, the device is the `bl-` word right after the channel word.

> `zazozon thugem blugewel vowurol.`
>
> z-Azozon | [th-LIVE | bl-camera] | v-walk
>
> "Azozon is walking, as I see on the camera."

> `zazozon thevum blugewel vowurol.`
>
> z-Azozon | [th-MEMORY | bl-camera] | v-walk
>
> "Azozon walked, as I remember from the camera."

### Practice {#beginner-practice}

Short drills for Beginner. Try each item before opening **Show answer**.

**Setting:** a café patio

**New words:**

| English | Ageben | Cue |
|---------|--------|-----|
| *departure* | `vudurul` | 🛫 |
| *cry* | `vagamul` | 😭 |
| *fight* | `vuvuvul` | 🫯 |
| *eat* | `vozedal` | 🍴 from *cutlery* |
| *pour* | `vobuvul` | 🫗 |
| *MAY* | `thomam` | 💭 from *thought*: a balloon over the scene |
| *LIVE* | `thugem` | 👁️‍🗨️ from *attest*: seen at the scene |
| *MEMORY* | `thevum` | 🎣 from *fishing*: pulled up from memory |

**Review:**

| English | Ageben |
|---------|--------|
| *Azozon* | `azozon` |
| *Alazun* | `alazun` |
| *Ahelan* | `ahelan` |
| *pay* | `varal` |
| *wine* | `owudal` |
| *scream* | `vozumul` |
| *sandwich* | `edal` |
| *punch* | `vabuvul` |

#### English → Ageben {#beginner-english-to-ageben}

**1.** *Ahelan may be leaving Azozon.*

::: details Show answer
`zahelan thomam dazozon vudurul.`

z-Ahelan | th-MAY | d-Azozon | v-departure
:::

**2.** *Azozon may be fighting Alazun, I'll find out.*

::: details Show answer
`zazozon thomal dalazun vuvuvul.`

z-Azozon | th-MAY-find-out | d-Alazun | v-fight
:::

**3.** *Alazun may be crying, who knows.*

::: details Show answer
`zalazun thomar vagamul.`

z-Alazun | th-MAY-who-knows | v-cry
:::

**4.** *Alazun is pouring wine, I can see it.*

::: details Show answer
`zalazun thugem dowudal vobuvul.`

z-Alazun | th-LIVE | d-wine | v-pour
:::

**5.** *Could Ahelan be paying?*

::: details Show answer
`yel zahelan varal thomam.`

y-question | z-Ahelan | v-pay | th-MAY
:::

**6.** *Azozon paid, I remember it.*

::: details Show answer
`zazozon thevum varal.`

z-Azozon | th-MEMORY | v-pay
:::

#### Ageben → English {#beginner-ageben-to-english}

**1.** `zazozon thomam dowudal vobuvul.`

::: details Show answer
z-Azozon | th-MAY | d-wine | v-pour

*Azozon may be pouring wine.*
:::

**2.** `zahelan thomal vozumul.`

::: details Show answer
z-Ahelan | th-MAY-find-out | v-scream

*Ahelan may be screaming, I'll find out.*
:::

**3.** `yel zalazun vuvuvul thomal dazozon.`

::: details Show answer
y-question | z-Alazun | v-fight | th-MAY-find-out | d-Azozon

*Might Alazun be fighting Azozon? Let's find out.*
:::

**4.** `zazozon thomar dedal vozedal.`

::: details Show answer
z-Azozon | th-MAY-who-knows | d-sandwich | v-eat

*Azozon may be eating a sandwich, who knows.*
:::

**5.** `zahelan thomam dalazun vabuvul.`

::: details Show answer
z-Ahelan | th-MAY | d-Alazun | v-punch

*Ahelan may be punching Alazun.*
:::

**6.** `zahelan thevum dedal vozedal.`

::: details Show answer
z-Ahelan | th-MEMORY | d-sandwich | v-eat

*Ahelan ate a sandwich, I remember it.*
:::

#### Pick one {#beginner-pick-one}

**1.** *Azozon may be crying, I'll find out.* `zazozon thomal vagamul.` or `zazozon thomar vagamul.`

::: details Show answer
`zazozon thomal vagamul.`

z-Azozon | th-MAY-find-out | v-cry

**-l** commits to settling it; **-r** is a passing thought you are not pursuing.
:::

#### Fix it {#beginner-fix-it}

**1.** *Ahelan may be leaving.* (a guess, not a claim) <!-- lint: error -->`zahelan vudurul.`

::: details Show answer
`zahelan thomam vudurul.`

z-Ahelan | th-MAY | v-departure

Without **`thomam`**, the sentence reports that Ahelan is leaving.
:::

#### What changes {#beginner-what-changes}

**1.** `zahelan thugem varal.` / `zahelan thevum varal.`

::: details Show answer
z-Ahelan | th-LIVE | v-pay

z-Ahelan | th-MEMORY | v-pay

**LIVE** says Ahelan is paying while you watch. **MEMORY** says Ahelan paid and you remember seeing it.
:::
